newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe sees December Trenton Canyon gold.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe sees December Trenton Canyon gold.

text.p: Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp said the first gold production from the Lone Tree Complex is now expected in December.

Gold production at Trenton Canyon, located 11 miles south of the Lone Tree Mine near Valmy, Nev., will begin slightly ahead of the previously announced start-up in the first quarter 1997, chief executive Patrick M. James said.

"The pieces are falling into place for us to achieve our production growth targets in 1997 and 1998. Trenton Canyon is one piece of the total Lone Tree Complex, which includes the Lone Tree Mine, Lone Tree Flotation Project and Mule Canyon."

The company said the Lone Tree Complex began placing ore onto the heap leach pads at Trenton Canyon on October 15. The leaching of the ore and completion of the carbon column recovery circuit is scheduled for next month, Santa Fe said.
Trenton Canyon currently is mining material at a rate of 30,000 tons per day at the North Peak deposit.

Trenton Canyon is a conventional run-of-mine heap leach satellite operation of the Lone Tree Complex. In addition to the North Peak deposit, two other deposits on private and federal lands are proposed for open-pit development.

Santa Fe said production from these two other deposits requires approval of the plan of operations submitted to the federal Bureau of Land Management in March 1996, adding approval is expected in mid-1998.
Exploration at Trenton Canyon this year has consisted of drilling 140 holes to better define certain areas of mineralization, extend mineralization and explore new targets.
The company said a new zone of shallow oxide mineralization is being encountered in the Valmy area.

A second target, referred to as the Hollywood Zone, is also under investigation and seven drill holes have intercepted a high-angle zone of near surface oxide mineralization with grades between 0.03 and 0.13 ounce of gold per ton in intercepts 40 to 105 feet thick. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
